children: Oura Inc., the maker of the Oura Ring health-tracking wearable and related subscription platform, filed for an initial public offering on the Nasdaq. The company plans to list under the ticker “OURA.” The filing shows strong recent growth, driven by hardware sales and recurring membership revenue, though specific pricing and offering size were not disclosed.

Oura is a consumer health technology company built around the Oura Ring, a finger-worn wearable designed for continuous, 24/7 measurement and an accompanying subscription that delivers personalized insights across sleep, activity, stress, heart health, and women’s health. The platform combines proprietary hardware, an AI-driven software stack, and a privacy-first infrastructure to translate high-fidelity, longitudinal biometric signals into actionable guidance for everyday decisions.

The company generates revenue primarily through hardware sales of the Oura Ring and recurring membership subscriptions (Oura Membership). Hardware anchors adoption and is designed to recover customer acquisition costs, while the high-retention subscription provides recurring, high-margin revenue. Oura differentiates through its finger-based signal quality, research-led product development, and a growing ecosystem of partnerships (e.g., Dexcom, Natural Cycles, ResMed, Lumeris/Essence Healthcare, Strava) that expand use cases and integrate Oura data across health journeys. Distribution is omnichannel—direct-to-consumer and wholesale retail partners—supported by strong word-of-mouth and a product-led growth model.
: Management cites a serviceable addressable market exceeding $90 billion across fitness trackers, health coaching, digital care management, digital therapeutics, and connected biosensors.
: Global wearable shipments totaled ~212 million units in the 12 months ended June 30, 2026, with Oura representing ~2% by units.
: Category-defining smart ring leader with 5.0 million Paid Members and a large longitudinal biometric dataset.
: Apple, Google (Fitbit), Samsung, Garmin, Whoop, and other wrist-based and software-only health platforms.

: Shift toward preventative and proactive health, rising out-of-pocket healthcare spending ($557 billion in 2024), and rapid advances in AI and biometric sensing enabling continuous, personalized insights.
: 5.0 million Paid Members as of June 30, 2026
: Products available in approximately 8,400 retail doors globally
: Sold in 56 markets; less than 20% of hardware revenue generated outside the U.S. for the nine months ended June 30, 2026

: Ecosystem includes Dexcom, Natural Cycles, ResMed, Lumeris/Essence Healthcare, Maven Clinic, Strava, Counsel Health, American Express, and major retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, Target, Costco, Walmart, Harrods, John Lewis, and JB Hi-Fi
: Rings Sold—3.6 million in the 12 months ended June 30, 2026; 3.1 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026; 2.3 million in FY 2025

: Median wear time ~23 hours/day (Q3 FY2026); DAU-to-MAU ~65%; Weighted-Average 12-Month Paid Member Retention ~85%; ~40% of new members acquired organically; U.S. aided brand awareness ~38% (Q3 FY2026); ~72% of members are women
: 74% year-over-year for the nine months ended June 30, 2026
, Chief Executive Officer - Former President of Momentive (SurveyMonkey); prior leadership roles at HomeAway, Linden Lab, and Adobe.
, Executive Chairman - Founder and Managing Partner of Lateralus Holdings; investing and board experience across technology and advanced manufacturing.
, Chief Financial Officer - Former CFO and CEO at Headspace; earlier finance leadership roles at Citigroup, Nomura, and Lehman Brothers.
, Chief Operating Officer - Former executive at Hewlett-Packard; extensive experience in engineering, R&D, and operations.
: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, Allen & Company LLC, Jefferies

: General corporate purposes including technology development, working capital, operating expenses and capital expenditures, and to satisfy anticipated tax withholding and remittance obligations related to RSU net settlement.
